subject: Request: temporary completion grace window for nightly async SKU inference
messages:
From: Carlos Mendez <carlos.mendez@nimbusretail.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 28 Mar 2027 15:24:00 -0700
Subject: Request: temporary completion grace window for nightly async SKU inference

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for supporting us on the integration. Late last week we saw a sustained surge in our order ingestion that pushed a number of nightly SKU enrichment jobs into long-tail processing. The jobs in question are the async inference batch that populates SKU embeddings and tags for our search/recommendation pipeline.

We attached a short request PDF with logs — essentially asking if Redwood can provide a temporary completion grace window (+3 hours) for nightly async jobs for our account while we complete a behind-the-scenes ETL re-shard. We want to avoid kills/retries that create duplicates downstream; idempotency is important.

Requested scope: 2027-03-29 -> 2027-04-12
Requested change: accept job completion up to +3 hours beyond the normal SLA window for nightly batches; no automatic chargeback for transient misses during the window.

Questions for you:
- Is a temporary tolerance like this feasible without a formal contract amendment?
- What controls do you need from our side to ensure safe retries/duplicates?

Appreciate a quick thumbs up or list of requirements so we can move forward.

Best,
Carlos
Director, Platform Operations
Nimbus Retail

Attachment: nimbus_sla_extension_request.pdf
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Mendez <carlos.mendez@nimbusretail.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary completion grace window for nightly async SKU inference

Carlos — thanks for the clear note and the PDFs. I started a quick internal thread to evaluate risk and operational guardrails.

Internal summary for visibility (short):
- Customer asks for a 2-week +3hr completion tolerance for nightly async batch jobs (account NIM-2027-07).
- Concern: long-running jobs increase chance of duplicate downstream writes unless idempotency tokens/dedupe are present.
- Proposed immediate mitigations I can put in place if we approve:
  * Require per-job idempotency_token header from Nimbus for all nightly jobs (we can enforce at API gateway).
  * Temporary retry policy: exponential backoff with max 3 retries and a job-level terminal state to avoid infinite requeue.
  * Fallback path: if job cannot complete by +6 hours, route to smaller model variant (faster) or mark as 'degraded' for manual review.
  * Monitoring: create a per-job SLA dashboard, alerts if >5% of nightly jobs exceed original SLA.
  * Credit: propose rolling credits if >10% windows missed during the tolerance period.

Laura / Rishi — can you both chime in on contract/legal implications and technical risk? If you both okay, I will confirm the temporary tolerance with Nimbus and request the idempotency headers and a short integration test.

I attached a small sample logs file (they included it) to help triage.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: sample_run_logs_20270327.txt
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 11:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary completion grace window for nightly async SKU inference

Stephanie — quick commercial/legal points:

- Short answer: we can often grant operational tolerances for limited windows without a full contract amendment, but we should document it as a one-off SLA amendment addendum (simple email addendum) that specifies the dates, acceptance criteria, and credit formula. I will have Legal prepare a one-paragraph addendum.

- Billing/credits: Finance prefers an objective rule (e.g., credit = proportion of missed successful jobs beyond 10% threshold). Keep it simple to avoid disputes.

- Customer-facing fallback: I like the smaller-model fallback idea; recommend we enumerate allowed fallbacks (list model variants) in the addendum so they have transparency.

Rishi — can you confirm technical requirements for idempotency enforcement and the feasibility of automated rollback to a faster model if a job stalls? Also, we should capture any increased support burden for SRE/on-call.

If both approve today I will draft the short addendum and send to Carlos for signature (email acceptance).

— Laura
Director, Enterprise Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 31 Mar 2027 08:52:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary completion grace window for nightly async SKU inference

Laura / Steph — technical sign-off with constraints:

I reviewed the logs and ran a risk matrix with infra and runtime leads. We can safely allow a temporary completion tolerance with the following mandatory controls:

1) Idempotency token: every batch job must include an idempotency_token (UUID) at submission. The gateway will reject jobs without it. This ensures dedupe at apply time.

2) Dedup window: enforce a 48-hour dedupe retention for job outcomes to prevent late replays from creating duplicates in downstream stores. We will store light-weight job outcome metadata in Redis (key: job:<id>:outcome).

3) Retry policy: adopt exponential backoff with jitter, max 3 retries per job. Retries after the max must mark job as FAILED and emit a high-severity alert (pager).

4) Fallback model: configure automatic fallback to model variant rwd-small-v2 if job duration exceeds original SLA + 4 hours. The fallback will run in a reduced accuracy but provides completion.

5) Observability: create a per-account dashboard (latency distribution, completion ratio, idempotency hits) and a short-lived runbook for triage. We will instrument traces and expose a job-status endpoint the customer can poll.

6) Expiration: tolerance window expires 2027-04-12 23:59 UTC unless extended by written agreement.

I will allocate one SRE on-call rotation for the first 48 hours after the change goes live. If during that period we see >15% of jobs using fallback model, we auto-revoke the tolerance and revert to default SLA (with customer notification).

Given these controls, I approve the temporary tolerance. Stephanie — please confirm you will require the idempotency token and that Nimbus will accept the fallback model list. Laura — please prepare the one-paragraph addendum.

— Rishi
Director, Production Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Mendez <carlos.mendez@nimbusretail.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Apr 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary completion grace window for nightly async SKU inference

Carlos — good news. We can approve a temporary, timeboxed completion tolerance for the nightly async jobs under the terms below. Please reply to this email to accept; we'll consider your reply an addendum to the contract for the dates below.

Approved terms (summary):
- Window: 2027-03-29 -> 2027-04-12 (expires 2027-04-12 23:59 UTC)
- Tolerance: up to +3 hours beyond normal completion window; fallback behavior to rwd-small-v2 enforced at +4 hours if job still outstanding
- Required from Nimbus: per-job idempotency_token (UUID) on submission; acceptance test before 2027-03-30 23:59 UTC to validate tokens and job-status polling
- Retries: exponential backoff with max 3 retries; jobs that exceed retries are marked FAILED and alerted to on-call
- Dedup retention: 48 hours for job outcome metadata
- Monitoring: Redwood will create a per-account SLA dashboard and alerts; SRE rotation assigned for first 48 hours
- Credits: objective credit rule if >10% of nightly jobs miss even the extended window; Finance will calculate per-addendum formula
- Revocation: if fallback usage >15% during the tolerance window, tolerance will be revoked and we notify you immediately

Next steps for Nimbus:
1) Confirm acceptance by replying to this message (that reply will act as the addendum signature).
2) Provide one sample job submission with idempotency_token and verify job-status polling (we'll provide an endpoint and a short integration test).

We will send the one-paragraph addendum from Legal for clarity, but your reply here will suffice to enact the tolerance immediately.

Thanks — we aim to keep your pipeline healthy while limiting operational risk.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
